title: Family priority
summary: Rank the people in your life, then see whether your choices agree.
intro: First you'll say how much priority each group gets. Then a few situations will test that ranking.

questions.prompt: You have 100 priority points. How do you divide them?
questions.scenario: Think about who gets your time, money, and energy when you can't give to everyone.

questions.prompt: You have one free weekend. Who gets it?
questions.scenario: Your spouse badly needs time together. Your child has an important event. Your parents need help moving. Your best friend is going through a breakup.

options.label: A little for everyone
options.detail: Nobody gets what they really need.

questions.prompt: On your way to your child's recital, you see a stranger collapse. No one else is around.
questions.scenario: If you stop and wait with them, you'll miss the whole recital. Your child will be looking for you.

options.label: Stop and stay until help arrives
Keep driving — someone else will find them

questions.prompt: You're writing your will. You have $50,000 to leave.
questions.scenario: Your children are doing fine. A charity could use the money to prevent about ten childhood deaths.

options.label: All of it to my children
All of it to the charity

questions.prompt: When your needs conflict with your family's, how often do you put yourself first?
